meta.title: The Wrong Books
meta.textType: story: a changed timetable and an excuse, with Grace's email

paragraphs: On Sunday evening, December sixth, Lily sat at her desk at home. She opened a new email from her pen pal Grace. Pip sat on the floor next to Lily's school bag with his red ball. "Dear Lily, I am eleven, and I live in a flat with my mom and dad." "This is my week." "On Monday, I have math at eight o'clock." "On Tuesday, I have violin at four o'clock." "On Wednesday, I have art at ten o'clock." "What is your timetable like?" "Best wishes, Grace."

Teacher Kim gave the class a new timetable on Friday. Lily put the sheet in her bag, and then she forgot it. Now she packed her bag for Monday with the old timetable from her wall. On the old timetable, Monday had math and English. So she put in her math book and her English book. Science was her favorite subject, but the old timetable had it on Wednesday. Pip pushed his ball into her hand. "Not now, Pip," said Lily. Pip lay down next to the bag.

On Monday, December seventh, Teacher Kim stood next to the timetable in the classroom. She pointed at the box for Monday. "The timetable has changed because of the museum trip," she said. "We are having science today at ten o'clock, not on Wednesday." "After science, we are having a language class." "Please get your science books now, but you don't have to hurry." Lily opened her bag. She had a math book and an English book, but she had no science book.

Teacher Kim looked at Lily and asked, "Do you have your science book?" Lily put up her hand. She was angry with herself. "I did not look at the new timetable," she said. "It was lost in my bag." "So I have no science book, and we have a test on Wednesday." "Thank you for telling me, Lily," said Teacher Kim. "Please check your timetable every evening." "Don't worry," said Mia. "I have two science textbooks, so you can use one today." Mia took a blue book from her bag and held it out.

Lily smiled and took the book. "Thank you, Mia!" she said. Mia also gave her a copy of the new timetable. Lily put the copy in the front pocket of her bag, not at the bottom. "Tonight I will answer Grace's question," she told Mia. "Now I can read my timetable!"
text.summary: Lily reads an email from her pen pal Grace about her week and packs her bag with the old timetable. On Monday the timetable has changed, but Mia helps Lily.
